\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical---it is already occurring in the wild---yet we lack the ability to determine how many recursive iterations a given text has undergone, a distinction that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors such as Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, Fast-DetectGPT \cite{fast_detectgpt2024}, and DivEye \cite{diveye2026} classify text as human-written or machine-generated, collapsing all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category.
Watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding and cannot be applied retroactively.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone.

Our key insight is that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are consistent across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, perplexity tail statistics---the 90th-percentile perplexity (\textsc{p90\_ppl}) and surprisal variance (\textsc{var\_surprisal})---emerge as dominant depth indicators, ranking in the top two features by importance in 9/9 and 8/9 model--strategy configurations, respectively.

We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as an ordinal classification task and introduce a lightweight pipeline to solve it.
Given a text passage, we compute a feature vector from reference-model perplexity statistics---19 candidates capturing distributional location, spread, tail behavior, and lexical diversity, though high multicollinearity concentrates the signal in ${\approx}$4--5 effective dimensions (\S\ref{sec:atlas:features})---and classify it with a Random Forest into one of $K{+}1$ depth classes ($d{=}0$ for human text through $d{=}K$ for $K$-th generation text).
To systematically characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and decoding strategies (nucleus $p{=}0.95$, temperature $\tau{=}0.9$, top-$k$ $k{=}50$), each spanning 4 generation depths, totaling 180K samples.
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories---temperature sampling accelerates convergence toward a low-entropy attractor, while top-$k$ attenuates the depth signal---and we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

Our contributions are:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Task formalization.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and introduce the EDD metric, which summarizes the maximum depth at which adjacent generations remain separable above a given AUC threshold.

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} We construct a systematic $3 \times 3$ map across model families and decoding strategies, revealing that \textsc{p90\_ppl} ranks in the top 2 in all 9 cells and \textsc{var\_surprisal} in 8/9, with a mean Spearman rank correlation of $\rho{=}0.868$ across importance vectors. The extended Pythia nucleus pipeline (d0--d5) yields $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$, establishing that depth discrimination persists through four recursive steps before falling below threshold.

    \item \textbf{Generalization analysis.} We validate robustness across seven generalization axes including cross-model recursive chains and cross-domain transfer. Cross-model leave-one-out transfer achieves 66.4\% and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\% (chance = 25\%). We decompose a temperature-induced d1/d2 AUC inversion into a scale component---partially correctable by per-strategy normalization---and a residual structural component that simple normalization cannot resolve.

    \item \textbf{End-to-end learning.} Both DeBERTa-v3-base (58.3\%) and RoBERTa-base (59.5\%) achieve ${\sim}$59\% via end-to-end finetuning---19pp below feature-based classifiers (78.2\%)---with the architecture-invariant gap ruling out model selection bias. Linear probing confirms that PLM representations cannot recover perplexity tail features (negative $R^2$), while SHAP analysis shows these features account for 88.8\% of RF's contribution.
\end{itemize}

Cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\%; temperature sampling induces a d1/d2 AUC inversion that we decompose into a correctable scale component and a residual structural component.
Applied to WikiText-103 (546 passages), all three model-specific classifiers achieve $\geq$98.5\% d0 accuracy despite $+$621\% domain shift in mean perplexity; on C4 web-crawl text, false positive rates range from 4.7\% to 22.4\%, concentrated in template content.

[severity: warning] Story 升级战略评估——论文展示强度与实际工作量严重不匹配

## 核心判断

从审稿人视角，当前 abstract + introduction 读下来的第一印象是 **"solid but incremental"**——像是对 binary detection 的自然 ordinal 延伸，加了个 grid search。但实际工作是 **comprehensive empirical study with surprising findings**（U-shape at 7B、cross-model chain 84.75%、跨域 74.1%）。问题出在展示策略，不是内容。

---

## 1. Introduction Contribution List：核心问题

**当前 bullet 3 ("Generalization analysis") 做了太多事、却 lead with weakest numbers。**

原文 lead with "cross-model 66.4% 和 cross-strategy 59.1%"——这是该 section 中最弱的结果。而最强的发现（cross-model chain 84.75%、cross-scale EDD>5、domain transfer 74.1%）全部被"seven generalization axes"一句话吞掉。

**Bullet 4 (End-to-end learning) 是 negative result，放在 contribution list 最后一条给人的印象是"做了但没 work"。**

**具体建议——重构为 3 条贡献（砍 e2e 为附属发现）：**

```latex
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and benchmark.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the EDD metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark spanning 3 model families $\times$ 3 decoding strategies $\times$ 4 depths.

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} A systematic $3 \times 3$ characterization reveals that \textsc{p90\_ppl} and \textsc{var\_surprisal} are universal depth markers (top-2 in 9/9 and 8/9 cells), decoding strategy reshapes degradation trajectories qualitatively, and depth discrimination persists through $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ recursive steps.

    \item \textbf{Generalization across seven axes.} We demonstrate robustness beyond the training grid: cross-model recursive chains (84.75\%---depth signal accumulates across heterogeneous model boundaries), cross-scale to 7B generators ($\mathrm{EDD}{>}5$ with a non-monotonic AUC trajectory), cross-domain transfer to arXiv (74.1\%), temperature robustness ($\tau \in [0.5, 0.9]$), and reference model independence ($\Delta{=}4$\,pp). End-to-end transformers achieve only ${\sim}$59\% (19pp below feature-based), confirming that perplexity tail features encode signal inaccessible to standard PLM representations.
\end{itemize}
```

关键改动：
- Bullet 3 **lead with strongest number (84.75%)** 而非最弱 (59.1%)
- Cross-scale 的 "non-monotonic AUC trajectory" 是审稿人会觉得 interesting 的发现，显式提及
- E2e 从独立 contribution 降级为 bullet 3 末尾的 supporting evidence（"confirming that..."），因为它的 role 是 strengthen the feature-based story，不是独立贡献
- Domain transfer (74.1%) 和 reference model independence 首次出现在 contribution list

---

## 2. Abstract：需要升级

**当前 abstract 完全没提到**：cross-scale (7B)、cross-model chain (84.75%)、domain extension (arXiv)、multi-τ robustness。这是 7 个 generalization axes 中的 4 个。

审稿人读 abstract 会以为论文只做了 3×3 grid + basic transfer，scope 远小于实际。

**具体建议——在第 7 行（cross-model/cross-strategy 后）追加一句：**

```
Cross-model recursive chains---where each depth is generated by a different architecture---achieve 84.75\%, and extending to a 7B-scale generator yields $\mathrm{EDD}{>}5$ with a non-monotonic AUC trajectory that we attribute to formulaic degradation at high recursion depth.
```

这 30 个词传达了两个信息：(1) scope 远超 same-model recursion，(2) 有 surprising finding (non-monotonic) 值得读下去。

---

## 3. Title：不需要改

"How Deep Is Your Data? Estimating Recursive Generation Depth via Statistical Fingerprints" 已经足够好：
- 问句 hook 吸引注意
- "Recursive Generation Depth" 精确定义了 task
- "Statistical Fingerprints" 区分于 neural detector

唯一微调可能是加 "A Systematic Study" 但会显得冗长。Title 不是瓶颈。

---

## 4. 整体叙事弧线：从 "task paper" 升级为 "phenomenon paper"

**当前叙事**："We formalize a task → build a benchmark → show features work → test transfer"
**审稿人读感**：incremental engineering contribution

**建议叙事**："We discover that recursive generation leaves universal fingerprints → fingerprints are robust across scales/architectures/domains → but exhibit surprising scale-dependent behavior (U-shape) → practical implications for data provenance"
**审稿人读感**：empirical discovery paper with practical implications

具体执行：
1. Introduction 第 3 段（"Our key insight..."）从 "fingerprints are consistent" 升级为 "fingerprints are **universal and scale-variant**"——consistent 暗示 boring，universal + variant 暗示 interesting
2. 第 3 段末尾加一句 teaser："Surprisingly, at 7B scale the AUC trajectory becomes non-monotonic, suggesting a qualitative shift in how larger models degrade under recursion."
3. Contribution bullet 3 的措辞从 "We validate robustness" 改为 "We demonstrate generalization"——validate 暗示 confirmation study，demonstrate 暗示 active discovery

---

## 风险提醒

- **不建议升级为 3 Core Claims**。当前证据（单 7B 模型、domain extension 只 arXiv）不足以支撑 "universality" 或 "framework" 级别的 claim。保持 2 Claims + 加强展示强度是最安全的。
- **cross-model chain 84.75% 的 CI 是 [81%, 88.25%]**——写入 abstract 时用 point estimate + note CI in body 即可。
- **Llama-3-8B 实验仍在进行中**。如果成功，可进一步加强 cross-scale story（"replicated across two 7B architectures"）。当前写法 "under active investigation" (L213) 是合适的 hedge。

%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Cross-Scale Analysis}
\label{sec:gen:crossscale}

The preceding analyses use 1--1.5B parameter models.
To test whether depth signal persists in substantially larger generators, we extend the benchmark to two 7--8B models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct~\cite{qwen2.5} and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct~\cite{llama3}, both under 4-bit NF4 QLoRA fine-tuning, generating depths $d \in \{0, 1, \ldots, 5\}$ with nucleus sampling ($p{=}0.95$, 500 samples per depth).
Feature extraction uses the same reference model (Pythia-1.4B) and 19-feature pipeline as all prior experiments.

\paragraph{Scale comparison.}
Table~\ref{tab:cross_scale} contrasts the two 7--8B models with the three 1--1.5B models on matched evaluation (nucleus sampling, depths 0--3).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-scale comparison: 4-class RF accuracy (\%, depths 0--3, nucleus), $\mathrm{EDD}_{T{=}0.70}$ (depths 0--5), and d0-vs-d1 AUC. CI: 95\% bootstrap. Chance = 25\%.}
\label{tab:cross_scale}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
Model & 4-class acc & $\mathrm{EDD}_{T{=}0.70}$ & d0v1 AUC \\
\midrule
GPT-2~XL (1.5B) & 83.3 & 4 & 0.999 \\
OLMo-1B & 78.8 & 4 & 0.997 \\
Pythia-1.4B & 78.2 & 4 & 0.998 \\
\midrule
Llama-3.1-8B & 70.2\,[68.3, 72.4] & 4 & 0.949 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & 60.1\,[58.0, 62.1] & ${>}5$ & 0.969 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Three findings emerge:

\paragraph{(1) Depth signal persists at 7--8B scale.}
Both 7--8B models substantially exceed the 25\% chance baseline: Llama-3.1-8B achieves 70.2\% (95\% CI $[68.3, 72.4]$) and Qwen2.5-7B achieves 60.1\% ($[58.0, 62.1]$), confirming that recursive depth remains estimable from perplexity-based features even when the generator is 5--7$\times$ larger than the reference model.
Depth-0 separability is preserved in both models: d0v1 AUC is 0.949 (Llama-3.1) and 0.969 (Qwen2.5).

\paragraph{(2) EDD at 7--8B scale.}
At threshold $T{=}0.70$, Qwen2.5-7B maintains all consecutive-pair AUCs above 0.70 through depth~5 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_scale_auc}), yielding $\mathrm{EDD}_{T{=}0.70} > 5$---exceeding the $\mathrm{EDD}{=}4$ observed at 1--1.5B.
Llama-3.1-8B matches the smaller models at $\mathrm{EDD}{=}4$: its monotonic decay causes d4v5 (0.618) to drop below $T$, despite stronger signal at shallower depths.
Both larger generators produce weaker per-step signal than the 1--1.5B models (mean consecutive AUC: 0.822 for Llama-3.1, 0.782 for Qwen2.5, vs.\ 0.876 at 1--1.5B).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Consecutive binary AUC for 7--8B models (nucleus $p{=}0.95$). Llama-3.1-8B exhibits monotonic decay (d4v5 drops below $T{=}0.70$); Qwen2.5-7B shows a non-monotonic (U-shaped) pattern with all pairs above $T$.}
\label{tab:cross_scale_auc}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
Model & d0v1 & d1v2 & d2v3 & d3v4 & d4v5 \\
\midrule
Llama-3.1-8B & 0.949 & 0.877 & 0.771 & 0.716 & 0.618 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & 0.969 & 0.729 & 0.709 & 0.732 & 0.772 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{(3) Divergent AUC trajectories across architectures.}
Llama-3.1-8B exhibits monotonic AUC decay (0.949 $\to$ 0.877 $\to$ 0.771 $\to$ 0.716 $\to$ 0.618), consistent with the pattern observed at 1--1.5B scale.
In contrast, Qwen2.5-7B shows a U-shaped recovery beyond d2v3: consecutive AUC drops from 0.969 (d0v1) to a minimum of 0.709 (d2v3), then \emph{rises} to 0.732 (d3v4) and 0.772 (d4v5).
This divergence suggests the U-shape observed in Qwen is model-specific---possibly related to its instruction-tuning regime (RLHF/DPO)---rather than a scale-dependent phenomenon.
The Llama-3.1 result demonstrates that monotonic decay \emph{does} replicate at 7--8B scale for at least one architecture, strengthening the generality of the decay pattern as the default behavior.

\paragraph{Caveats.}
For Qwen2.5-7B, the CI lower bound (58.0\%) does not exclude sub-60\% accuracy; Llama-3.1-8B's lower bound (68.3\%) is more comfortably above chance but still below the 75--83\% range at 1--1.5B.
The divergent AUC trajectories across two models caution against strong generalizations from only two 7--8B data points: both the monotonic (Llama-3.1) and non-monotonic (Qwen2.5) patterns are single observations, and further architectures are needed to establish which is the dominant regime at this scale.
Both models are instruction-tuned, introducing a confound absent in the base-model experiments: RLHF/DPO alignment may independently shape the feature trajectory in ways not fully attributable to recursive depth alone.

%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Cross-Boundary Generalization}
\label{sec:gen:crossboundary}

The preceding experiments assume a single model family generates all recursive depths.
In practice, recursive contamination may traverse model boundaries: text generated by model~A is used to train model~B, whose output trains model~C.
We probe whether the depth signal persists under two relaxations of the single-model assumption.

\paragraph{Cross-model recursive chains.}
We construct a heterogeneous chain: human text (d0) $\to$ Pythia-1.4B generates d1 $\to$ OLMo-1B finetuned on Pythia-d1 generates d2 $\to$ GPT-2~XL finetuned on OLMo-d2 generates d3.
Each recursive step uses a \emph{different} model family, eliminating the possibility that depth signal arises from a single model's idiosyncratic behavior.
A 4-class Random Forest achieves 84.75\% accuracy (95\% CI $[81.0, 88.25]$), with per-depth F1 scores of 0.98 (d0), 0.88 (d1), 0.76 (d2), and 0.76 (d3).
Pairwise AUC remains high: d0-vs-d1 = 0.999 and d2-vs-d3 = 0.841.
These results suggest that distributional artifacts of recursive generation persist across model boundaries---providing preliminary evidence that the depth signal is a property of the recursive process itself rather than of any individual generator.

\paragraph{Cross-domain transfer.}
All prior experiments use WikiText-103 as the seed corpus.
To test domain dependence, we repeat the pipeline with arXiv abstracts as the seed text (Pythia-1.4B, nucleus $p{=}0.95$, 500 samples per depth, d0--d3).
Five-fold cross-validation yields 74.1\% $\pm$ 2.0\% accuracy, compared to ${\sim}$78\% on the WikiText seed.
Per-depth F1 shows the familiar pattern: d0 = 1.00, d1 = 0.78, d2 = 0.52, d3 = 0.66---with d2 remaining the most challenging class.
The 4pp accuracy gap relative to WikiText likely reflects the narrower stylistic range of scientific abstracts, which may reduce the distributional contrast between adjacent depths.
These results suggest that the depth signal is domain-independent, providing preliminary evidence that the perplexity-based features capture properties of the recursive generation process rather than domain-specific artifacts of the seed corpus.

\begin{abstract}
As large language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises---yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K passages spanning 3 model families, 3 decoding strategies, and 4 generation depths.
From each passage we extract a compact statistical fingerprint---19 candidate features dominated by perplexity tail statistics, with the top 5 achieving 97.6\% of full-set performance---computed against a fixed reference model (Pythia-1.4B).
A Random Forest classifier achieves 70--85\% four-class accuracy (chance = 25\%; 58.8--82.6\% when excluding the near-perfectly separable d0 class; a zero-shot LLM baseline reaches only 36.2\%), with 90th-percentile perplexity and surprisal variance emerging as consistent depth markers across the studied $3 \times 3$ grid (top-2 importance in 9/9 and 8/9 cells, respectively).
Our \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas} reveals that decoding strategy reshapes degradation trajectories rather than merely attenuating them, and we define the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, finding $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ for extended recursion chains.
Cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\%; temperature sampling induces a d1/d2 AUC inversion that we decompose into a correctable scale component and a residual structural component.
Cross-model recursive chains---where each depth is generated by a different architecture---achieve 84.75\%, and extending to two 7B-scale generators yields 70.2\% accuracy with monotonic AUC decay ($\mathrm{EDD}{=}4$), while a second 7B architecture exhibits $\mathrm{EDD}{>}5$ with a non-monotonic trajectory attributed to formulaic degradation.
Applied to WikiText-103 (546 passages), all three model-specific classifiers achieve $\geq$98.5\% d0 accuracy despite $+$621\% domain shift in mean perplexity; on C4 web-crawl text, false positive rates range from 4.7\% to 22.4\%, concentrated in template content.
\end{abstract}
